Stage 01

Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, especially Articles 3, 4, 7, 8, 14 and 25; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May approving the implementing regulation of Law 10/2010; Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishing the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership; Spanish Commercial Code provisions on ownership and control disclosures; Law 10/2010, Article 4, generally identifies the beneficial owner as the natural person or persons ultimately owning or controlling, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of the capital or voting rights, or otherwise exercising control. If no such person is identifiable after reasonable investigation, the senior managing official is treated as the fallback beneficial owner, with the investigation documented.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A Spanish Sociedad Limitada must have a registered office in Spain under the Companies Act, Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July, particularly Articles 9 and 10. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable if it is a genuine address at which statutory notices can be received and corporate records or management activity can be supported. A mailbox-only arrangement is inadequate. For logistics fleet dispatch and telematics SaaS, the company should maintain demonstrable operational substance proportionate to its activity, including contracts, accounting records, technical infrastructure arrangements, data-protection governance, customer-support capability, and evidence of effective management. A virtual office does not establish tax residence, permanent-establishment protection, transfer-pricing substance, employment compliance, or eligibility for regulated payment or communications activities.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry, Madrid) for name certification; Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) of the registered office for inscription; publication in the Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME).

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Spanish Companies Act, 'LSC'); core provisions: Art. 4 (minimum capital), Arts. 20-29 (incorporation), Art. 33 (public deed), Art. 124 (registered office) and Arts. 209-233 (administrators); supplemented by Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura pública de constitución (Notarial Deed of Incorporation) containing the bylaws (estatutos), executed before a Spanish notary and formally inscribed in the Provincial Commercial Registry.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 41 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Minimum capital of EUR 3,000 (approx. USD 3,250) per Art. 4 LSC, fully subscribed and paid up in cash at incorporation. The funds must be deposited in a Spanish bank account opened in the name of the 'SL en formación', evidenced by a bank deposit certificate (certificado de depósito) produced to the notary; alternatively the funds may be delivered to the notary for deposit. No escrow account is required. Funds are released to the administrator only after registration.

Funding & unlock path:

Paid-in capital rule: Minimum capital of EUR 3,000 (approx. USD 3,250) per Art. 4 LSC, fully subscribed and paid up in cash at incorporation. The funds must be deposited in a Spanish bank account opened in the name of the 'SL en formación', evidenced by a bank deposit certificate (certificado de depósito) produced to the notary; alternatively the funds may be delivered to the notary for deposit. No escrow account is required. Funds are released to the administrator only after registration.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft

(2) The draft bylaws (estatutos) are adopted, their corporate purpose covering information technology, fleet telematics and logistics software services. (3) The registered office is fixed at [Address, City, Province], Spain. (4) [Name] is appointed sole administrator (administrador único) for an indefinite term with full powers of representation. (5) The administrator is authorized to execute the public deed, obtain the provisional NIF, deposit the capital, register the company and complete all filings, including the definitive NIF and social security registration.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Official Electronic Portal: https://www.agenciatributaria.gob.es/

E-government filing portal

Spanish SL entities obtain NIF (Código de Identificación Fiscal) upon incorporation via AEAT registration. Foreign entities with Spanish operations register for tax identification. Process requires filing Modelo 036 or 037 through the AEAT online portal, submission of corporate documents including articles of association, and issuance of NIF as the statutory TIN for all tax obligations including VAT.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — Spanish SL entities obtain NIF (Código de Identificación Fiscal) upon incorporation via AEAT registration. Foreign entities with Spanish operations register for tax identification. Process requires filing Modelo 036 or 037 through the AEAT online portal, submission of corporate documents including articles of association, and issuance of NIF as the statutory TIN for all tax obligations including VAT.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

No check-the-box elections available under Spanish law. Entities are subject to entity-level taxation under the general corporate income tax regime (Impuesto sobre Sociedades). Optional regimes may apply for specific activities; hybrid mismatch rules are governed by EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) and Spanish transposition legislation.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

€30,000 in annual taxable turnover

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods upon verified proof of export. For offshore services, 0% rate or exemption applies if services are provided to non-EU customers without utilizing a Spanish permanent establishment. Eligibility requires documentation confirming the export or offshore character of the transaction.

  • Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate

Mandatory electronic invoicing for all VAT-registered taxpayers since 2023 using Facturae standard or equivalent digital format. Real-time fiscal clearance and digital stamping (sello electrónico) required via AEAT integration for compliant issuance and reporting; non-compliance triggers penalties and potential suspension of operations.

Zero-rating or VAT refund claims must be substantiated with supporting documentation. Fraudulent or unsubstantiated claims result in retrospective clawback of undue tax benefits plus interest and surcharges, administrative fines from €1,000 to €300,000 or higher, and potential criminal liability for intentional misconduct.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain is a Eurozone member state within the EU single market and EEA; the euro is fully convertible and both current account and capital account operations are liberalised under Articles 63-65 TFEU. No exchange control authorisation, prior licence, or central bank permit is required for inbound equity injections, outbound trade settlements, or dividend repatriation. The only frictions are fiscal and administrative: Spanish corporate income tax at the statutory 25% rate; non-resident dividend withholding tax at the domestic 19% rate (potentially reduced to 0% or a treaty rate under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the shareholder qualifies); and post-transaction statistical declarations to the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores and the Banco de España. Profit remittance is legally unrestricted once the annual accounts are approved and the distribution resolution is notarised and recorded in the Registro Mercantil.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender rule, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to repatriate export receivables to a Spanish account. Exporters may lawfully retain EUR or foreign currency proceeds in any bank account worldwide, subject to Spanish transfer-pricing, thin-cap, and anti-deferral rules. The sole binding condition is statistical: reportable cross-border payment operations (typically those exceeding EUR 50,000 in value, or monthly aggregated flows above the Banco de España threshold) must be declared through the reporting bank within the legally prescribed period of 30 days from settlement, with supporting invoices and contracts retained for a minimum of five years.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting together with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise for foreign investment registrations, and the SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias) for anti-money laundering supervision of credit institutions and payment entities.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Stripe Fit: High

Rated HIGH for secondary collection and disbursement efficiency, but MEDIUM-LOW as a sole treasury rail. Cross-border EMIs passported under the EU E-Money Directive 2009/110/EC and PSD2, and duly registered with the Banco de España for activity in Spain, may lawfully open EUR IBAN operational accounts for the SL, enabling low-cost SEPA collections (including Stripe Billing settlement routing) and competitive FX conversion for USD-denominated SaaS subscriptions. Critical legal constraints: EMIs are not authorised to issue documentary credits, cannot provide overdrafts/trade finance, do not offer segregated capital escrow services, and may trigger enhanced scrutiny from the resident tax authorities if the SL's formal books and records reside outside the Spanish banking system. Therefore the EMI channel must be configured as a sweeper account with nightly concentration to the tier-1 Spanish operational account, never as the main treasury hub.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Non-resident corporate shareholder with an opaque multi-tier holding chain

Root cause: Non-resident corporate shareholder with an opaque multi-tier holding chain

Defense evidence: Dossier comprising the shareholder's certificate of incorporation (apostilled and sworn-translated into Spanish), the updated table of the SL's ultimate beneficial owners filed with the Registro Mercantil in the form required by the bank, the shareholder register of the owning entity, audited financial statements of the parent for the last two years, bank references from the shareholder's primary lender, identity documents of each UBO, an executed source-of-wealth declaration, and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for the holding structure.
Sole director (administrador único) who is a non-resident without a Spanish NIE or with no verifiable tax residence

Root cause: Sole director (administrador único) who is a non-resident without a Spanish NIE or with no verifiable tax residence

Defense evidence: Valid NIE certificate obtained from the provincial tax office, apostilled biometric passport page, certified copy of the foreign residence permit or public utility bill evidencing residential address, a certificate of no criminal record from the country of nationality (where required by the bank), the deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) and the appointment deed duly registered in the Registro Mercantil, and a notarised power of attorney granted to a Spanish tax resident for ongoing banking representations.
Principal collections flowing through third-party payment processors (Stripe Billing) and cross-border EMIs, creating uncertainty about the SL's effective treasury control and transaction origin

Root cause: Principal collections flowing through third-party payment processors (Stripe Billing) and cross-border EMIs, creating uncertainty about the SL's effective treasury control and transaction origin

Defense evidence: Executed commercial agreements with each payment processor identifying the SL as the merchant of record, a documented payment-flow diagram from end customer to processor to the SL's Spanish bank account, the SL's NIF and corporate registry certificate, twelve-month customer and transaction forecast distinguishing recurring Logistics-Tech SaaS fees from hardware-related pass-through charges, processor payout statements for the last six months, and a cash concentration policy letter instructing the processor to sweep balances daily to the tier-1 bank account in Spain.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Inbound capital injections from non-resident shareholders are executed either by SWIFT MT103 (for USD or any non-EUR currency) or by SEPA Credit Transfer (if the shareholder maintains a EUR account at an EEA bank), always crediting the SL's named operational or capital escrow account at the tier-1 Spanish bank. The wire narrative must carry the SL's NIF (B-number), the shareholder reference, and a compliant purpose narrative containing the European Balance of Payments conceptual code for direct investment capital (subscription of equity in a resident non-financial corporation). The bank will require supporting evidence: the notarised minutes of the shareholders' capital increase resolution, the certificate of payment of capital, the SL's updated articles of association, current UBO declaration, and the foreign investor's KYC record. The transaction must then be reported by the bank or the SL to the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores (when the non-resident shareholding reaches the statutory declaration threshold) and through the Banco de España Balance of Payments statistical return within 30 days after settlement; failure to file is an administrative infraction but does not invalidate the capital contribution or render the funds non-convertible.Within the SEPA zone, EUR-denominated trade and operating disbursements (cloud infrastructure, freight-tech partners, EU-based hardware suppliers) clear via SEPA Credit Transfer, including instant SEPA when required. For non-EUR and extra-EEA payments, the SL uses SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfers, with MT202 COV reserved for interbank or aggregate concentration movements. For inbound fleet-hardware procurement from third-country manufacturers (telematics devices, GPS modules, communication hardware), the SL may open an Irrevocable Documentary Letter of Credit at its tier-1 bank in favour of the supplier, with shipment documents negotiated through the beneficiary's bank; alternatively, goods payments below the LC threshold use documentary collection and direct MT103 against invoices. Each outbound payment must cite the applicable Spanish Balance of Payments purpose code (services/royalties or merchanting trade), and the bank will expect the underlying commercial contract, invoice, and, where applicable, customs documentation to remain on file for KYC and sanctions compliance review.Plain-vanilla EUR/USD FX forward with tenors up to 12 months backed by confirmed USD-denominated SaaS subscription receivablesEuropean-style purchased FX call options (EUR call/USD put) providing downside protection while preserving upside for receivables collectionsNon-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in selected Latin American currencies (ARS, BRL, CLP, MXN) via authorised Spanish banks to hedge logistics fleet operations or partner payables in those jurisdictionsCross-currency interest rate swap (CCIRS) to convert future USD debt proceeds or USD trade payables into EUR liabilities if the SL enters an offshore financing arrangement with its non-resident parentFX collar strategies combining purchased and written options for tightly quantified telematics fleet expansion exposure in non-EEA markets

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Rated HIGH for secondary collection and disbursement efficiency, but MEDIUM-LOW as a sole treasury rail. Cross-border EMIs passported under the EU E-Money Directive 2009/110/EC and PSD2, and duly registered with the Banco de España for activity in Spain, may lawfully open EUR IBAN operational accounts for the SL, enabling low-cost SEPA collections (including Stripe Billing settlement routing) and competitive FX conversion for USD-denominated SaaS subscriptions. Critical legal constraints: EMIs are not authorised to issue documentary credits, cannot provide overdrafts/trade finance, do not offer segregated capital escrow services, and may trigger enhanced scrutiny from the resident tax authorities if the SL's formal books and records reside outside the Spanish banking system. Therefore the EMI channel must be configured as a sweeper account with nightly concentration to the tier-1 Spanish operational account, never as the main treasury hub.
